functionWrapperSemantics: Synchronous entry-to-return and async entry-to-promise-settlement are inclusive; nested calls overlap. Async continuation CPU is not separately isolated.
limitations: Both WebKit reports remain incomplete because startup resources have one invalid record and no valid app-script timing. These records are preserved; no zero duration, expected hash substitution or complete attribution claim is invented.

All six fixed script-counter sets, readiness/frame callback clocks, full-profile and ten-editor workloads, source/script/binary/runtime identities and owned cleanup are verified. This bounded coverage does not repair the two incomplete whole observations.

WebKit initialize/readCore promise wall and renderAll synchronous counters are small relative to startup/frame delivery. The counters do not attribute unwrapped script work, async continuation CPU, style/layout/paint or browser/driver work to a specific function.
Frame observations are performance.now callback delivery times, not compositor or actual paint timestamps. Whole-job CPU includes the owned job and is not per-function CPU.

Script/resource interception and timing wrappers alter the diagnostic harness. A single synthetic fixture cohort does not establish causality, normal product acceptance, installed performance or repeat reliability.

Normal acceptance runs original application bytes. Previous Firefox sustained RSS and WebKit baseline latency failures remain open, along with signing, installed/native, eight-hour, managed-deployment and held investigations.
